The message delivers or links to an Android app package (.apk). Legitimate organizations never send apps over WhatsApp.
The message mentions a known brand but links to an unverified domain.
The domain looks similar to an official institution but is deceptive.
The link uses a raw IP address instead of a domain name.
The link hides its true destination using a URL shortener.
The website uses a domain extension frequently associated with scams.
The link uses foreign or lookalike characters to mimic a legitimate site.
The link was deliberately formatted to bypass security filters.
Claims to be government or police, but does not use an official .gov.in or .nic.in address.
The link uses a user-info trick to hide where it actually leads.
The website is on a verified blocklist of fraudulent addresses.
The sender wants you to move to a different platform or chat.
Asks for OTP, PIN, or password
Requests secret authentication codes. Banks and services never ask for your OTP.
Instructs you to download an app or remote control tool.
Asks for an upfront charge, fine, registration fee, or penalty.
UPI PIN to receive money trap
Claims you must enter a UPI PIN or scan a QR code to receive money. Entering your PIN always sends money, never receives it!
Asks for Aadhaar, PAN, or card details
Orders you not to tell family or police, or stay on call continuously.
Directs you to click an unverified link to update or reactivate services.
Requests moving from WhatsApp to Telegram.
Claims to be a contact on a new number asking for emergency funds.
Pressures you to act within hours to prevent rational thought.
Threat of account or SIM block
Threatens that your bank account, KYC, or phone service will be suspended.
Threat of arrest or legal action
Claims an arrest warrant, police FIR, or digital arrest.
Threat of electricity or utility cutoff
Threatens immediate disconnection of electricity tonight.
Promises large cash prizes or lucky draws you never entered.
Work from home / part-time job lure
Offers unrealistic daily earnings for simple video likes or reviews.
Promises doubled money, stock tips, or guaranteed profits.
Advertises predatory or fake instant loan approval.
Claims unclaimed rewards or cashbacks are waiting.
Sent from a personal mobile number while claiming to represent a bank, government, or company.
Claims a parcel is held due to incomplete address.
Urges immediate payment for a vehicle challan.
Uses an event invitation lure to deliver malware.
Uses generic salutations typical of mass fraud campaigns.
Uses invisible characters or foreign lookalike letters to evade detection.
Sent from an unsaved number not in your contacts.
Sent from a foreign country code
Sent from an international number outside India.
You have never received messages from this number before.
Legitimate banks, government bodies, and utilities send messages via registered TRAI headers, never personal 10-digit mobile numbers.
Header brand mismatch or promotional ask
The message content claims to represent an institution different from the sender header, or a promotional SMS requested sensitive payment or verification.
The overall pattern of phrasing closely matches known scam campaigns.

Aggressive battery optimization on some devices may stop DUARF from checking incoming notifications. Follow the steps below for your device brand.
1. Open device Settings > Apps > Manage Apps > DUARF 2. Enable \'Autostart\' (or Background Autostart) 3. Under Battery saver, select \'No restrictions\'
1. Open device Settings > Battery > Background usage limits > \'Never sleeping apps\' and add DUARF 2. Open Settings > Apps > DUARF > Battery and choose \'Unrestricted\'
1. Open device Settings > Apps > App Management > DUARF > Battery usage 2. Turn on \'Allow background activity\' and \'Allow auto-launch\'
1. Open device Settings > Battery > Background power consumption management 2. Select DUARF and choose \'High background power usage\'
You can change this any time in Settings.
DUARF checks messages in every supported language, whatever you choose here.
